To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypoxia and endothelins are involved in the proliferation of pulmonary vascular smooth muscle cells and that hypoxia may induce the autocrine of endothelins in PASMC.
ET-1 stimulates proliferation of PASMC through endothelin receptor subtype-A (ETA), and the proliferation of PASMC is further increased when the cells are exposed to hypoxia.
ET-1 and hypoxia stimulate DNA synthesis in cultured bovine PASMC and that hypoxia may stimulate the release of ET-1 from cultured PASMC.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the proliferative effect of ET- 1 on cultured PASMC, the role of autocrine of ET-l in the proliferation and the cooperative effect between hypoxia and autocrine of ET -1 on the proliferation of PASMC.
the mitogenic effect and the autocrine mechanism of hypoxia on PASMC.
the mitogenic effect and autocrine of ET1 on PASMC, which may be one of the important mechanisms of pulmonary hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypoxia and the autocrine of ET in PASMC are responsible for the proliferation of PASMC.
hypoxia and endothelins may be the major factors involved in the development of pulmonary artery remodelling.
hypoxia and/or ET-1 could stimulate the proliferation of PASMC, and the mechanism might be the autocrine of ET.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ET-1 and hypoxia stimulated the DNA synthesis of cultured PASMC and the effect of hypoxaemia was mediated by ET-1.
the ET-1 and ET-1 receptor subtype A are involved in the proliferation of PASMC under hypoxic condition and the mitogenic effect could be inhibited by some dilatory drugs.
hypoxia and endothelium-1 stimulate the proliferation of PASMC via an autocrine mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypoxia and the ET-1 system play an important role in PASMC proliferation.
hypoxia and endothelium-1 stimulate DNA synthetic activity in cultured PASMC, and this effect may be related to the autocrine of ET in PASMC.
hypoxia and endothelins are important factors in the proliferation of pulmonary artery smooth muscles.
